beats.say: Everton legend Duncan Ferguson is now a manager in the Irish League.
The BBC reports Glentoran have named him their new manager, after Declan Devine left in September.
As a striker he played for Dundee United, Rangers, Newcastle and Everton, and won seven caps for Scotland.
He then coached at Everton under Carlo Ancelotti and Rafael Benitez, and managed Forest Green Rovers and Inverness.
Glentoran have 23 league titles, but the last came in 2009, and their latest trophy was the County Antrim Shield.
So can Ferguson bring title number 24 home?
